You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls. The target takes a –15-foot penalty, and the Escape DC is 19.

equipment.name: Grasping Snare
entries: You rig vines and ropes to hold a creature in place. The first creature to enter the square must attempt a DC 26 Reflex save with the following effects.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 minute or until it {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes} (DC 26).
{@b Failure} The creature is {@condition Immobilized|PC1|immobilized} for 1 round, then takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 minute. Both effects end early if it Escapes (DC 26).
{@b Critical Failure} The creature is immobilized for 1 minute or until it Escapes (DC 26).

equipment.name: Graveroot
entries: The opaque white sap from the graveroot shrub clouds the mind.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 19 Fortitude; {@b Maximum Duration} 4 rounds
{@b Stage 1} 1d8 poison damage (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} 1d10 poison damage and {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied} 1 (1 round); Stage 3 2d6 poison damage and stupefied 2 (1 round)

equipment.name: Guise of the Smirking Devil
entries: This ice-blue half-mask is adorned with a wicked silver grin that covers only the wearer's mouth. You gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Intimidation|PC1} checks.

{@b Activate}{@b —Hideous Wail} {@as 2} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}, {@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} The mask emits a soul-chilling scream that deals 6d10 void damage to each living creature in a 20-foot emanation (DC 25 basic Fortitude save).

equipment.name: Guise of the Smirking Devil (Greater)
entries: This ice-blue half-mask is adorned with a wicked silver grin that covers only the wearer's mouth. You gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Intimidation|PC1} checks.

{@b Activate}{@b —Hideous Wail} {@as 2} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}, {@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} The mask emits a soul-chilling scream that deals 6d10 void damage to each living creature in a 20-foot emanation (DC 25 basic Fortitude save).

The item bonus to Intimidation is +3. Activating a {@i greater guise of the smirking devil} casts {@spell Wails of the Damned|PC1|wails of the damned} (DC 41), affecting all living creatures in the area.

equipment.name: Hail of Arrows Snare
entries: When a creature enters the snare's square, it releases hundreds upon hundreds of carefully prepared arrows, blanketing a 20-foot radius around the snare's square with massive arrow fire that deals 18d6 piercing damage. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 37 basic Reflex save.

equipment.name: Hampering Snare
entries: You arrange brambles, wires, sticky goo, or other materials to interfere with a creature's movement. The square with this snare as well as three adjacent squares (to form a 10-foot-by-10-foot area) become difficult terrain when the first creature enters the snare's square. The difficult terrain affects the creature's movement right away, including its movement into the triggering square, and it lasts for 1d4 rounds after the snare is triggered. A creature can use an Interact action to clear the difficult terrain out of a single square early.

equipment.name: Helm of Zeal
entries: This elaborate helmet is emblazoned with the divine symbols of a deity chosen when the helmet was crafted. You gain a +2 item bonus to that deity's Divine Skill.

{@b Activate}{@b —Rally to the cause} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a devotion spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.

{@b Activate}{@b —Divine Fervor} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Trigger} You've just used your champion's reaction; {@b Effect} You gain an additional reaction you can use only for your champion's reaction. You lose this reaction if you don't use it by the start of your next turn.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're a champion of the deity represented by the helmet.

equipment.name: Helm of Zeal (Greater)
entries: This elaborate helmet is emblazoned with the divine symbols of a deity chosen when the helmet was crafted. You gain a +2 item bonus to that deity's Divine Skill.

{@b Activate}{@b —Rally to the cause} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a devotion spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.

{@b Activate}{@b —Divine Fervor} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Trigger} You've just used your champion's reaction; {@b Effect} You gain an additional reaction you can use only for your champion's reaction. You lose this reaction if you don't use it by the start of your next turn.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're a champion of the deity represented by the helmet.
The item bonus to the deity's Divine Skill is +3. You can activate Divine Fervor once per hour.

equipment.name: Hemlock
entries: Concentrated hemlock is a particularly deadly toxin that halts muscle action—including that of the victim's heart.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 38 Fortitude; {@b Onset} 30 minutes; {@b Maximum Duration} 60 minutes
{@b Stage 1} 16d6 poison damage and {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled} 2 (10 minutes)
{@b Stage 2} 17d6 poison damage and enfeebled 3 (10 minutes)
{@b Stage 3} 18d6 poison damage and enfeebled 4 (10 minutes)

equipment.name: Hobbling Snare
entries: You rig vines, ropes, or wires to cinch tight around a creature that triggers this snare. The first creature to enter the square must attempt a DC 20 Reflex save.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 minute or until it {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes} (DC 18).
{@b Failure} As success, but the penalty is –10 feet.
{@b Critical Failure} As success, but the penalty is –20 feet.

equipment.name: Holy Chain
entries: This suit of {@i +2 resilient {@equipment Chain Mail|PC1|chain mail}} is made of fine white links of a strange and slightly translucent pale metal, and the sleeves and skirt are fashioned into smaller trails that resemble feathers. Unlike normal chain mail, holy chain has no Speed reduction, its armor check penalty is 0, and its Bulk is 1.

You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against fiends. You appear radiant while you wear the armor, giving you a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks against all creatures except fiends.
If you're {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy}, you're {@condition Drained|PC1|drained} 2 while wearing holy chain. You can't recover from this condition while wearing the armor.

{@b Activate}{@b —Celestial Flight} {@as 1} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} The armor sprouts glowing wings that grant you a fly Speed of 30 feet. The wings shed bright light in a 40-foot radius (and dim light to the next 40 feet). The wings fade away after 10 minutes.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're holy.

equipment.name: Hunter's Bane

stats.Trigger: A {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} or {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected} enemy hits you with an attack

entries: This talisman is a ring of dried, interwoven pieces of straw. When you activate the {@i hunter's bane}, you sense the exact location of the attacker. It becomes {@condition Observed|PC1|observed} by you if it was {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} from you or becomes hidden from you if it was {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected}. If the attacker is behind lead, the {@i hunter's bane} has no effect.

equipment.name: Incense of Distilled Death
entries: This black incense smells of fresh earth and ash. You activate the incense by lighting it, whereupon it fills a 10-foot emanation with oily smoke and potent void energy. Undead creatures gain fast healing 4 while in the area; though this healing comes from void energy, it doesn't negatively impact living creatures. Once lit, the incense burns for 1 minute, and it can't be extinguished.

equipment.name: Infiltrator's Accessory
entries: This elegant {@i +1 striking {@equipment Sword Cane|PC1|sword cane}} serves equally well as both a fashionable accessory and a hidden weapon suitable for high-society events where weapons aren't typically permitted.

{@b Activate}{@b —Hide Magic} {@as 1} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Effect} You twist the sword cane's hilt, magically merging the blade into the cane. While the blade is merged, it can't be drawn and gains the benefits of a 3rd-rank {@spell Disguise Magic|PC1|disguise magic} spell to appear non-magical. Passive observers can't attempt a check to notice the cane is anything more than a mundane, if superb, fashion accessory. Those carefully examining it can discern the cane is more than it appears, but doing so is extremely difficult (DC 30 Perception). Activating the sword cane again releases the blade, allowing it to be drawn normally.

equipment.name: Instant Evisceration Snare
entries: When a creature enters the snare's square, the snare releases an unbelievable arsenal of blades at the creature, dealing 18d8 piercing damage (DC 42 basic Reflex save).

equipment.name: Iron Cudgel
entries: This miniature club is typically affixed to a weapon by an iron chain. When you activate the cudgel, you use {@feat Brutal Finish|PC1}, as the fighter feat. You must meet the normal requirements, including those of the {@trait Press|PC1|press} trait.
If you have the Brutal Finish feat, add an additional weapon damage die on a success or a failure to the normal results.

equipment.name: Iron Equalizer
entries: This small iron band has a shifting weight that helps equalize the affixed weapon's balance. When you activate it, you use {@feat Certain Strike|PC1}, as the fighter feat. You must meet the normal requirements, including those of the {@trait Press|PC1|press} trait.
If you have the Certain Strike feat, the failure effect increases to deal the weapon's normal damage.

equipment.name: Jade Bauble
entries: This bit of jade is usually carved in the shape of a duelist, or sometimes a multi-armed creature. When you activate the bauble, it magically draws the attention of foes. Until the start of your next turn, enemies within the reach of the weapon the talisman is affixed to are {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}.

equipment.name: Juggernaut Mutagen
entries: Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous.
{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points.
{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

equipment.name: Juggernaut Mutagen (Greater)
entries: Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous.
{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points.
{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.
The bonus is +3, you gain 30 temporary Hit Points, and the duration is 1 hour. When you roll a success on a Fortitude save, you get a critical success instead.

equipment.name: Juggernaut Mutagen (Lesser)
entries: Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous.
{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points.
{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.
The bonus is +1, you gain 5 temporary Hit Points, and the duration is 1 minute.

equipment.name: Juggernaut Mutagen (Major)
entries: Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous.
{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points.
{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

The bonus is +4, you gain 45 temporary Hit Points, and the duration is 1 hour. When you roll a success on a Fortitude save, you get a critical success instead, and your critical failures on Fortitude saves become failures instead.

equipment.name: Juggernaut Mutagen (Moderate)
entries: Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous.
{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points.
{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.
The bonus is +2, you gain 10 temporary Hit Points, and the duration is 10 minutes.

equipment.name: King's Sleep
entries: King's sleep is an insidious long-term poison that can seem like a disease or even death from natural causes on a venerable target. The {@condition Drained|PC1|drained} condition from king's sleep is cumulative with each failed save and can't be removed while the poison lasts.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 41 Fortitude; {@b Onset 1} day
{@b Stage 1} drained 1 (1 day)
{@b Stage 2} drained 1 (1 day)
{@b Stage 3} drained 2 (1 day)

equipment.name: Leadenleg
entries: Once injected, this synthetic toxin sinks into the extremities, numbing them nearly to paralysis.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 20 Fortitude; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 rounds
{@b Stage 1} 1d10 poison damage and –5-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} 2d6 poison damage and –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 round)
{@b Stage 3} 2d6 poison damage and –20-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 round)

equipment.name: Lethargy Poison
entries: Lethargy poison is commonly used in hit-and-run tactics by attackers who want their victims alive; the ambusher retreats until the poison sets in and the victim falls {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious}. Further exposure to lethargy poison doesn't require the target to attempt additional saving throws; only failing a saving throw against an ongoing exposure can progress its stage.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 18 Fortitude; Maximum Duration 4 hours
{@b Stage 1} {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed} 1 (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} slowed 1 (1 minute)
{@b Stage 3} unconscious with no Perception check to wake up (1 round) {@b Stage 4} unconscious with no Perception check to wake up (1d4 hours)

equipment.name: Mariner's Splint
entries: This suit of {@i +1 {@equipment Splint Mail|PC1|splint mail}} is worn by veteran sailors aboard warships who want as much protection as possible but still need to remain mobile enough to {@action Climb|PC1|climb} up rigging or {@action Swim|PC1|swim} should the need arise. The plates are arranged for maximum flexibility and the undercoat of padded armor is often no more than a cotton shrift. The armor grants you a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks to Climb or Swim and increases the distance you move when you successfully {@action Climb|PC1} or {@action Swim|PC1} by 5 feet.

equipment.name: Marking Snare
entries: This snare is often used to mark intruders for later tracking or identification. When you create this snare, you must decide whether to make it a dye or a scent marker. Either type of marking grants a +2 circumstance bonus to {@action Track|PC1} the creature for up to 24 hours or until the dye or scent is washed off (requiring at least a gallon of water and 10 minutes of scrubbing). A creature that enters a square of the snare must attempt a DC 17 Reflex save.
{@b Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Failure} The snare marks the creature.
{@b Critical Failure} The snare marks the creature, and the creature is {@condition Blinded|PC1|blinded} until the end of its next turn.

equipment.name: Matchstick
entries: An alchemical substance applied to one end of this tiny wooden stick ignites when struck against a rough surface. Creating a flame with a matchstick is much faster than creating a flame with flint and steel. You can ignite it and touch it to a flammable object as part of the same Interact action. A matchstick remains lit for 1 round, after which it's consumed and extinguished.

equipment.name: Medusa's Scream
entries: The ghastly visage of a slain medusa's head stares out from this {@equipment Steel Shield|PC1|steel shield} (Hardness 13, HP 52, BT 26). The shield comes with a thick leather cover to conceal the head.

{@b Activate}{@b —Petrifying Gaze} {@as 2} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}, {@trait Visual|PC1|visual}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You reveal the medusa's face, focusing its gaze on one creature within 30 feet. The shield casts a DC 30 petrify spell with a range of 30 feet.
{@b Craft Requirements} The initial raw materials must include the head of a medusa.

equipment.name: Medusa's Scream (Greater)
entries: The ghastly visage of a slain medusa's head stares out from this {@equipment Steel Shield|PC1|steel shield} (Hardness 13, HP 52, BT 26). The shield comes with a thick leather cover to conceal the head.

{@b Activate}{@b —Petrifying Gaze} {@as 2} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}, {@trait Visual|PC1|visual}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You reveal the medusa's face, focusing its gaze on one creature within 30 feet. The shield casts a DC 30 petrify spell with a range of 30 feet.
{@b Craft Requirements} The initial raw materials must include the head of a medusa.
A {@i greater medusa's scream} (Hardness 15, HP 60, BT 30) has a frequency of once per hour for its activation instead of once per day, and the DC is 35.

equipment.name: Mindfog Mist
entries: Mindfog mist can be used to undermine spellcasters, as its effect on a victim's mental faculties are swift and powerful.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 35 Fortitude; {@b Onset} 1 round; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 rounds
{@b Stage 1} {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied} 2 (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} {@condition Confused|PC1|confused} and stupefied 3 (1 round)
{@b Stage 3} confused and stupefied 4 (1 round)

equipment.name: Mistform Elixir
entries: A faint mist emanates from your skin, making you concealed for the listed duration. As usual, if you become {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} when your position is still obvious, you can't use this concealment to {@action Hide|PC1} or {@action Sneak|PC1}.

equipment.name: Mistform Elixir (Greater)
entries: A faint mist emanates from your skin, making you concealed for the listed duration. As usual, if you become {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} when your position is still obvious, you can't use this concealment to {@action Hide|PC1} or {@action Sneak|PC1}.
The duration is 5 minutes.

equipment.name: Mistform Elixir (Lesser)
entries: A faint mist emanates from your skin, making you concealed for the listed duration. As usual, if you become {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} when your position is still obvious, you can't use this concealment to {@action Hide|PC1} or {@action Sneak|PC1}.
The duration is 3 rounds.

equipment.name: Mistform Elixir (Moderate)
entries: A faint mist emanates from your skin, making you concealed for the listed duration. As usual, if you become {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} when your position is still obvious, you can't use this concealment to {@action Hide|PC1} or {@action Sneak|PC1}.
The duration is 1 minute.

equipment.name: Mudrock Snare
entries: Fired clay covers a shallow pit of thin mud interspersed with fragile vials of a quick-drying agent. The first creature to step into the square breaks through the clay and sinks into the pit, fracturing the vials and releasing the chemicals that harden the mud. That creature must attempt a DC 29 Fortitude save as the mud solidifies over its legs.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes a –5-foot circumstance penalty to its Speed for 1 minute or until it {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes} (DC 27).
{@b Failure} The creature is {@condition Stunned|PC1|stunned} 2, and it takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speed for 1 minute or until it Escapes (DC 27).
{@b Critical Failure} The creature is stunned 3, and it's {@condition Immobilized|PC1|immobilized} for 1 minute or until it Escapes (DC 27).

equipment.name: Nauseating Snare
entries: You position particularly foul substances to splash over a creature. The first creature to enter the square must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude saving throw.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature becomes {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened} 1.
{@b Failure} The creature becomes sickened 2.
{@b Critical Failure} The creature becomes sickened 3.

equipment.name: Nethershade
entries: Distilled from the Netherworld, this oily substance imposes tenebrous effects. The {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled} condition from nethershade lasts for 24 hours.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 29 Fortitude; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 rounds
{@b Stage 1} 2d6 void damage and 2d6 poison damage (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} 3d6 void damage, 2d6 poison damage, and enfeebled 1 (1 round)
{@b Stage 3} 3d6 void damage, 3d6 poison damage, and enfeebled 2 (1 round)

equipment.name: Nettleweed Residue
entries: Concentrated sap of stinging weeds makes an effective toxin.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 27 Fortitude; {@b Onset} 1 minute; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 minutes
{@b Stage 1} 3d6 poison damage (1 minute)
{@b Stage 2} 4d6 poison damage (1 minute)
{@b Stage 3} 6d6 poison damage (1 minute)

equipment.name: Oil of Dynamism
entries: This fine golden oil comes in a small blue canister. Carefully spreading the oil over an object turns it into an animated object of the same type. For example, sprinkling it on a statue makes an animated statue. If the animated object's level would be greater than 3, the oil struggles to animate it and ultimately fails.

This animated object has the {@trait Minion|PC1|minion} trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you Command it. You can issue a Command for the current turn as part of the activation. The object remains animated for 1 minute before falling inert. As usual, you can have a maximum of four minions under your control.

equipment.name: Oil of Dynamism (Greater)
entries: This fine golden oil comes in a small blue canister. Carefully spreading the oil over an object turns it into an animated object of the same type. For example, sprinkling it on a statue makes an animated statue. If the animated object's level would be greater than 3, the oil struggles to animate it and ultimately fails.

This animated object has the {@trait Minion|PC1|minion} trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you Command it. You can issue a Command for the current turn as part of the activation. The object remains animated for 1 minute before falling inert. As usual, you can have a maximum of four minions under your control.
You can animate an object with a level of 11 or lower.

equipment.name: Oil of Revelation
entries: This bright oil, first created by humans as a tool to help them fight in darkness, holds flecks of tiny gemstones in suspension and smells like a struck matchstick.

The first time a weapon coated with this oil damages a creature, the wound glows with light for 1 minute. If the creature is {@condition Invisible|PC1|invisible}, the light's position means it's merely {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} to creatures that would otherwise be unable to see it, rather than {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected}. The light also negates the {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} condition due to lighting conditions. If the coated weapon doesn't damage a creature within 1 hour, the oil sloughs off and loses its power.

equipment.name: Omnidirectional Spear Snare
entries: As soon as a creature enters the snare's square, the snare unleashes wickedly powerful spears at the creature from all directions, dealing 15d8 piercing damage (DC 37 basic Reflex save).

equipment.name: Onslaught Hide
entries: This {@i +1 resilient {@equipment Hide Armor|PC1|hide armor}} is decorated with the horns of many slain beasts. It has an armor check penalty of –1 instead of –2. When you use the {@feat Sudden Charge|PC2} class feat while wearing this armor, your {@action Strike|PC1} deals an additional 1d8 damage.

equipment.name: Philosopher's Stone
entries: An {@class Alchemist|PC2|alchemist} with the {@feat Craft Philosopher's Stone|PC2} feat adds the formula for this item to their formula book. This allows them to create a philosopher's stone once per month during their daily preparations using advanced alchemy. Unlike other items created with advanced alchemy, the philosopher's stone remains potent for 1 month or until the alchemist creates a new one. This is the only way to create a philosopher's stone.

At a glance, a philosopher's stone appears to be an ordinary, sooty piece of natural rock. Breaking the rock open with a {@action Force Open|PC1} action (DC 35) reveals a cavity at the stone's heart. The cavity is lined with a rare type of quicksilver that can transmute base metals into precious metals or create an elixir of rejuvenation. To use the quicksilver, you must be legendary in {@skill Crafting|PC1} and have the {@feat Alchemical Crafting|PC1} feat. You can then use the stone's quicksilver for one of two effects.

items: You can apply the stone's quicksilver to an {@trait Infused|PC2|infused} {@equipment Elixir of Life|PC2|true elixir of life} using an Interact action. This turns the elixir into an infused {@equipment Elixir of Rejuvenation|PC2|elixir of rejuvenation} instantaneously. This doesn't require any crafting time or additional materials.

You can spend up to a month of {@rule Downtime|PC1|downtime} applying the quicksilver either to iron to create silver or to lead to create gold. Treat this as a 20th-level task to {@action Earn Income|PC1} using Crafting, except that you create 500 gp worth of your chosen metal per day on a success or 750 gp worth per day on a critical success.

equipment.name: Potion of Disguise
entries: Upon imbibing this potion, you take on the appearance of a specific type of creature for 2d12 hours. The type of creature is determined when the potion is created. For example, you might have a {@i potion of elf disguise} or {@i potion of frog disguise}. Drinking the potion doesn't impart the knowledge of how long the effect lasts; the GM rolls the duration in secret.

The disguise doesn't change your traits or statistics, nor does it give you any of the special abilities of the creature you're imitating. It might affect what items you can hold or wear (for example, your new form might lack opposable thumbs). The potion shrinks you down to a minimum of size Small or maintains your size if the creature is your size or larger. For example, if you are Medium and drink a potion of fire giant disguise, you'll take on the appearance of a fire giant but remain Medium. The creature has to be of a specific kind, such as “leopard” or “lion” rather than just “cat,” or “fire giant” or “ogre” rather than just “giant,” but the potion can't cause you to mimic a specific individual creature.

The effects of this potion use the same rules as the {@action Impersonate|PC1} activity of Deception. Onlookers always assume you're the chosen type of creature unless they're actively Seeking. You gain a +4 status bonus to your Deception DC against such Perception checks and add your level even if untrained.

The creature has to be of a specific kind, such as “leopard” or “lion” rather than just “cat,” or “fire giant” or “ogre” rather than just “giant,” but the potion can't cause you to mimic a specific individual creature.

The effects of this potion use the same rules as the {@action Impersonate|PC1} activity of Deception. Onlookers always assume you're the chosen type of creature unless they're actively Seeking. You gain a +4 status bonus to your Deception DC against such Perception checks and add your level even if untrained.

While drinking a {@i greater potion of disguise}, if you picture the specific form you want to transform into, the potion will change you into that form. You can attempt to Impersonate a specific individual, though you still need to roll Deception.

equipment.name: Potion of Disguise (Lesser)

stats.Craft Requirements: Initial raw materials must include a bit of blood, hair, or flesh of the creature the potion will allow the drinker to imitate.

{@b Craft Requirements} Initial raw materials must include a bit of blood, hair, or flesh of the creature the potion will allow the drinker to imitate.

equipment.name: Potion of Emergency Escape
entries: The stopper for a potion of emergency escape is crafted to easily snap open in dire circumstances. When you drink this potion, for 1 minute you become {@condition Fleeing|PC1|fleeing} from all hostile creatures you’re aware of. You gain a +40-foot status bonus to all Speeds as long as this fleeing condition lasts. You immediately {@action Stride|PC1}.

equipment.name: Potion of Retaliation
entries: A potion of retaliation is available in four varieties—acid, cold, electricity, and fire—each with a faint shimmer of the energy it contains. For 1 minute after drinking a {@i potion of retaliation}, you glow with a faint aura of that energy, and a creature that touches you (such as by making an unarmed attack or using a spell with a range of touch against you) takes damage of that type. The moderate, greater, and major versions also damage an adjacent creature that hits you with a melee weapon {@action Strike|PC1}.

equipment.name: Potion of Retaliation (Greater)
entries: A potion of retaliation is available in four varieties—acid, cold, electricity, and fire—each with a faint shimmer of the energy it contains. For 1 minute after drinking a {@i potion of retaliation}, you glow with a faint aura of that energy, and a creature that touches you (such as by making an unarmed attack or using a spell with a range of touch against you) takes damage of that type. The moderate, greater, and major versions also damage an adjacent creature that hits you with a melee weapon {@action Strike|PC1}.
The aura deals 3d6 damage.

For 1 minute after drinking a {@i potion of retaliation}, you glow with a faint aura of that energy, and a creature that touches you (such as by making an unarmed attack or using a spell with a range of touch against you) takes damage of that type. The moderate, greater, and major versions also damage an adjacent creature that hits you with a melee weapon {@action Strike|PC1}.
The aura deals 1d4 damage.

The moderate, greater, and major versions also damage an adjacent creature that hits you with a melee weapon {@action Strike|PC1}.
The aura deals 1 damage.

For 1 minute after drinking a {@i potion of retaliation}, you glow with a faint aura of that energy, and a creature that touches you (such as by making an unarmed attack or using a spell with a range of touch against you) takes damage of that type. The moderate, greater, and major versions also damage an adjacent creature that hits you with a melee weapon {@action Strike|PC1}.
The aura deals 2d4 damage.

equipment.name: Predictable Silver Piece
entries: This seemingly unremarkable, weathered silver coin bears the bust of an unnamed monarch on the face and a majestic bird on the tail. You can toss the coin without activating it, in which case it follows the normal laws of probability.

{@b Activate}{@b —Cheat Fate} {@as 1} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Effect} You rub your thumb on one side of the coin with the intent of slightly tweaking the strands of fate, then flip the coin into the air in a coin toss. No matter how the toss is resolved—letting the coin fall to the ground, slapping it down on the back of your hand, or catching it on your open palm—it always lands with the side you rubbed face up.

equipment.name: Prognostic Veil
entries: This gauzy purple veil is embroidered with symbols of divinatory significance. As your curse worsens, the veil ripples in an ever-increasing unseen wind. You gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Religion|PC1} checks.

{@b Activate}{@b —Remember the Future} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a revelation spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.

{@b Activate}{@b —Twist the Skeins of Fate} {@as r} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} oncer per day; {@b Trigger} An ally within 30 feet is about to attempt a saving throw; {@b Requirements} You have the {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} condition; {@b Effect} The ally gains a status bonus to the saving throw equal to the value of your cursebound condition.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're an oracle.

entries: This gauzy purple veil is embroidered with symbols of divinatory significance. As your curse worsens, the veil ripples in an ever-increasing unseen wind. You gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Religion|PC1} checks.

{@b Craft Requirements} You're an oracle.
The item bonus to Religion checks is +3. You can activate Twist the Skeins of Fate for an attack roll or a saving throw.

equipment.name: Quicksilver Mutagen
entries: You become swifter and nimbler but also fragile.

{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} checks, {@skill Stealth|PC1} checks, {@skill Thievery|PC1} checks, Reflex saves, and Dexterity-based attack rolls, and you gain the listed status bonus to your Speed.
{@b Drawback} You take damage equal to twice your level; you can't recover Hit Points lost in this way by any means while the mutagen lasts. You take a –2 penalty to Fortitude saves.

entries: You become swifter and nimbler but also fragile.

{@b Drawback} You take damage equal to twice your level; you can't recover Hit Points lost in this way by any means while the mutagen lasts. You take a –2 penalty to Fortitude saves.
The bonus to rolls is +3, the bonus to Speed is +15 feet, and the duration is 1 hour.

equipment.name: Quicksilver Mutagen (Lesser)
entries: You become swifter and nimbler but also fragile.

{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} checks, {@skill Stealth|PC1} checks, {@skill Thievery|PC1} checks, Reflex saves, and Dexterity-based attack rolls, and you gain the listed status bonus to your Speed.
{@b Drawback} You take damage equal to twice your level; you can't recover Hit Points lost in this way by any means while the mutagen lasts. You take a –2 penalty to Fortitude saves.
The bonus to rolls is +1, the bonus to Speed is +5 feet, and the duration is 1 minute.

equipment.name: Ration Tonic
entries: This slender vial appears to hold clean, clear water with a faintly fruity scent. Drinking a {@i ration tonic} magically nourishes you with the equivalent of a day's worth of food and water. The tonic has a subtle, pleasant taste, its particulars chosen when the potion is crafted.

equipment.name: Ration Tonic (Greater)
entries: This slender vial appears to hold clean, clear water with a faintly fruity scent. Drinking a {@i ration tonic} magically nourishes you with the equivalent of a day's worth of food and water. The tonic has a subtle, pleasant taste, its particulars chosen when the potion is crafted.
A {@i greater ration tonic} nourishes you for 1 week instead of 1 day, distributing the nourishment in a constant and healthy flow across the week.

equipment.name: Rending Snare
entries: Sharp metal jaws wind tightly into the pressure plate mechanism of this snare. When triggered, the jaws clamp shut and spin, damaging limbs in the process. The snare deals 10d8 piercing damage to the first creature to enter the square; that creature must attempt a DC 34 Reflex save.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes half damage and is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the end of its next turn.
{@b Failure} The creature takes full damage plus {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|2d6 persistent bleed damage}, and it becomes {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} 2 for 1 round.
{@b Critical Failure} The creature takes double damage plus 4d6 persistent bleed damage, and it becomes clumsy 2 for 1 minute.

equipment.name: Ring of Maniacal Devices
entries: This magic ring seems like simple tarnished brass, but it enhances your curiosity about traps and devices of all kinds. You can use an Interact action to pull a {@equipment Thieves' Toolkit|PC1|thieves' toolkit} from the ring. This toolkit appears in your hand and any part of it folds back into the ring if they would leave your possession. They grant you a +2 item bonus to Thievery checks to {@action Disable a Device|PC1} and to {@action Pick a Lock|PC1}, and the ring's insights grant you the same bonus to Crafting checks to {@action Craft|PC1} and {@action Repair|PC1} snares and traps.

{@b Activate}{@b —Fireball Trap} 10 minutes ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You create the effects of a rune trap ritual containing {@spell Fireball|PC1|fireball}. You can have only one trapped rune from a ring of maniacal devices active at a time, even if you have multiple rings, and the rune disappears if you lose your investiture in the ring.

equipment.name: Sanguine Pendant
entries: This clear crystal pendant contains a drop of blood from a sorcerer that expands and contracts as you cast spells. A {@i sanguine pendant} is associated with a specific sorcerer bloodline, and only sorcerers with that bloodline can invest this item. This item gains the trait matching the tradition of that bloodline. The pendant grants a +2 item bonus to both of your bloodline skills.

{@b Activate}{@b —Blood's Call} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a bloodline spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're a sorcerer with the associated bloodline.

{@b Craft Requirements} You're a sorcerer with the associated bloodline.
The item bonus to your bloodline skills is +3.

equipment.name: Sash of Prowess
entries: This humble sash can be worn around the waist or across the chest. A sash of prowess often bears a coloration or a pattern that represents the monastery in which you trained but can also sport religious symbology, such as the open hand of Irori. You gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} and {@skill Athletics|PC1} skill checks.

{@b Activate}{@b —Effortless Mastery} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Requirements} You succeed at an Acrobatics or Athletics skill check; {@b Effect} You critically succeed instead.

{@b Activate}{@b —Reserves of Inner Strength} {@as f} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a qi spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.
{@b Craft Requirements} You're a monk who can cast qi spells.

equipment.name: Scything Blade Snare
entries: This snare sends a powerful series of scything blades to slice through a creature entering the snare's square, dealing 10d8 slashing damage (DC 32 basic Reflex save).

equipment.name: Sea Touch Elixir
entries: This briny concoction alters the skin on your hands and feet. The spaces between your fingers and toes become webbed, granting you a swim Speed of 20 feet for the listed duration.

equipment.name: Sea Touch Elixir (Greater)

{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to Will saves and Perception, {@skill Medicine|PC1}, {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Religion|PC1}, and {@skill Survival|PC1} checks. This bonus improves when you attempt Will saves against mental effects.
{@b Drawback} You take a –1 penalty to attack rolls and save DCs of offensive spells, and a –1 penalty per damage die to all weapon, unarmed attack, and spell damage.

equipment.name: Shielding Salve
entries: This shimmering paste has many properties of a {@spell Shield|PC1|shield} spell. When you slather it onto a creature or object, the target gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC for 1 round. The first time a physical attack or a {@spell Force Barrage|PC1|force barrage} hits the target during that round, the oil prevents 5 damage from that attack or spell, and then the oil's effect ends.

equipment.name: Signaling Snare
entries: A subtle snare used in hunting or tracking, a signaling snare often consists of carefully prepared earth, piled sand or stones, specific arrangements of vegetation, and so forth. When a creature enters a square of a signaling snare, nothing happens to the creature, but instead it causes a small, unobtrusive disruption to the terrain that allows the snare's creator or another creature who knows what to look for to determine whether a creature of the appropriate size entered the square.

equipment.name: Silver Salve
entries: You can slather this silvery paste onto one melee or ranged weapon, or 10 pieces of ammunition. Silver salve spoils quickly, so you must use a vial all at once. For the next hour, the weapon or ammunition counts as silver instead of its normal precious material (such as cold iron) for any physical damage it deals.

equipment.name: Silvertongue Mutagen
entries: Your features become striking, and your voice becomes musical and commanding, though emotion clouds your reason.

{@b Benefit} You gain an item bonus to {@skill Deception|PC1}, {@skill Diplomacy|PC1}, {@skill Intimidation|PC1}, and {@skill Performance|PC1} checks. Your critical failures with any of these skills become failures instead.

{@b Drawback} You take a –2 penalty to {@skill Arcana|PC1}, {@skill Crafting|PC1}, {@skill Lore|PC1}, {@skill Occultism|PC1}, and {@skill Society|PC1} checks. Choose one skill in which you're trained; for the duration, you become untrained in that skill.

The bonus is +2, and the duration is 10 minutes.

equipment.name: Skinstitch Salve
entries: This sticky salve stubbornly holds wounds closed and encourages swift natural healing. You can activate the salve in either of the following ways.

{@b Activate}{@b —Administer Stitch} {@as 1} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Effect} You {@action Administer First Aid|PC1} without requiring healer's tools. You can either gain a +2 item bonus to the {@skill Medicine|PC1} check or use the salve's Medicine modifier of +13 instead of your own.

{@b Activate}{@b —Stitch Wounds} {@as f} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Trigger} You {@action Treat Wounds|PC1} or use {@feat Battle Medicine|PC1}; {@b Effect} You gain a +2 item bonus to the triggering {@skill Medicine|PC1} check. If you roll a success on the Medicine check, you get a critical success instead.

equipment.name: Slumber Arrow
entries: Sleep arrows often have shafts of deep blue or black, and their fletching is exceptionally soft and downy. An activated {@i sleep arrow} deals no damage, but a living creature hit by it grows lethargic and must attempt a DC 17 Will saving throw. On a failure, it takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round, and is also {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed} 1 for 1 round on a critical failure.
{@b Craft Requirements} Supply one casting of {@spell Sleep|PC1|sleep}.

equipment.name: Slumber Wine
entries: Slumber wine sees its greatest use in matters of social intrigue, where an absence can be more devastating than injury. Characters {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious} from slumber wine can't wake up by any means while the poison lasts, don't need to eat or drink while unconscious in this way, and appear to be recently dead unless an examiner succeeds at a DC 40 Medicine check.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 32 Fortitude; {@b Onset 1} hour; {@b Maximum Duration} 7 days
{@b Stage 1} unconscious (1 day)
{@b Stage 2} unconscious (2 days)
{@b Stage 3} unconscious (3 days)

equipment.name: Smoke Ball
entries: With a sharp twist of this item, you instantly create a screen of thick, opaque smoke in a burst centered on one corner of your space. All creatures within that area are {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed}, and all other creatures are concealed to them. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind.

equipment.name: Smoke Ball (Greater)
entries: With a sharp twist of this item, you instantly create a screen of thick, opaque smoke in a burst centered on one corner of your space. All creatures within that area are {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed}, and all other creatures are concealed to them. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind.
The radius of the burst is 20 feet.

The radius of the burst is 5 feet.

equipment.name: Snagging Hook Snare
entries: This snare snags a creature with its wicked metal hooks. The first creature to enter the square takes 5d8 piercing damage and 5d8 slashing damage, with a DC 29 basic Reflex save. On a critical failure, the hooks piercing its flesh make the creature immobilized until it successfully {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes} (DC 29).

equipment.name: Snake Oil
entries: You can apply snake oil on a wound or other outward symptom of an affliction or condition (such as sores from a disease or discoloration from a poison). For the next hour, the symptom disappears, and the {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded} or afflicted creature doesn't feel as if it still has the wound or affliction, though all effects remain. A creature can uncover the ruse by succeeding at a DC 17 Perception check, but only if it uses a {@action Seek|PC1} action to specifically examine the snake oil's effects.

equipment.name: Spellguard Blade
entries: The guard of this {@i +1 striking {@equipment Main-gauche|PC1|main-gauche}} is inscribed with eldritch glyphs that guard against magic. When you're benefiting from the circumstance bonus to AC from this weapon's {@trait Parry|PC1|parry} trait, you also apply that circumstance bonus to your saving throws against spells that target you.

equipment.name: Spider Root
entries: A paste made by mashing the fine, threadlike roots of a certain creeper vine, spider root renders a victim clumsy and maladroit.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 28 Fortitude; {@b Onset 1} minute; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 minutes
{@b Stage 1} 3d6 poison damage and {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} 1 (1 minute)
{@b Stage 2} 4d6 poison damage and clumsy 2 (1 minute)
{@b Stage 3} 6d6 poison damage and clumsy 3 (1 minute)

equipment.name: Spider Venom
entries: This spider venom erodes a target's defenses.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 22 Fortitude; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 rounds
{@b Stage 1} 1d10 poison damage and {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened} 1 (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} 1d12 poison damage, {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} 1, and sickened 2 (1 round)
{@b Stage 3} 2d6 poison damage, clumsy 2, and sickened 3 (1 round)

equipment.name: Spike Snare
entries: This basic snare consists of hidden spikes that rely on a creature's momentum to lacerate or potentially impale it as it enters the snare's square, dealing 2d8 piercing damage. The creature must attempt a DC 17 basic Reflex saving throw.

equipment.name: Spiritsight Crossbow
entries: This {@i +1 striking ghost touch {@equipment Crossbow|PC1|crossbow}} has an array of crystalline lenses and silver fittings along the stock and feels strangely light.

{@b Activate}{@b —Ethereal Vision} {@as 1} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per minute; {@b Effect} You aim through the crossbow's crystalline lenses, gaining imprecise vision onto the Ethereal Plane with a range of 60 feet in addition to your normal senses until the end of your turn. You can sense through objects in the Universe this way, and the sense is precise for detecting creatures. Because this sense detects spiritual energy, a creature that's immune to spirit can't be detected in this way.

{@b Activate}{@b —Ethereal Shot} {@as 1} {@b Requirements} Ethereal Vision is active; {@b Effect} You Strike with the {@i spiritsight crossbow}. This shot travels through the Ethereal Plane, allowing it to pass through and ignore cover from physical objects within the range of your Ethereal Vision.

equipment.name: Staff of Impossible Visions
entries: This bizarre staff is made from oak, capped with a cluster of eye-shaped gemstones that seem to move and undulate at the corner of your vision. While wielding the staff, you can peer through the eyes on the staff rather than your own, using your normal visual senses (including any benefits of spells like {@spell See the Unseen|PC1|see the unseen}). You can maneuver the staff to see things around corners, at higher elevations, or in places where the staff can fit but your head can't. This doesn't provide sufficient line of effect to target creatures around corners. The eyes are as vulnerable as your eyes and can be affected by anything that alters your vision, such as a blinding flash of light.
{@b Activate} Cast a Spell; {@b Effect} You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
{@b Craft Requirements} Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.

equipment.name: Staff of Providence
entries: A large, stylized symbol of an eye adorns the top of this wooden staff, representing the watchful eye of the divine powers. The bearer of the staff can guide and protect, seeing bounties and tragedies that could befall them in the future. When wielding this staff, you gain a +1 item bonus to Survival checks to {@action Sense Direction|PC1} or {@action Subsist|PC1} and to Religion checks to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1}.

equipment.name: Stalker Bane Snare
entries: This snare explodes in a burst of cloying powder that can cling to a creature stepping into its square. A creature that enters the square of a stalker bane snare must attempt a DC 20 Reflex save.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.

{@b Success} Powder sticks to the target, causing it to leave behind telltale footprints. Being {@condition Invisible|PC1|invisible} makes the target {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden}, rather than {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected}, to creatures that could see it if it weren't invisible.

{@b Failure} Powder clumps on the target, constantly flaking away. Being invisible makes the target concealed, rather than hidden or undetected, to creatures that could see it if it weren't invisible.
{@b Critical Failure} As failure, and the creature is {@condition Blinded|PC1|blinded} until the end of its next turn.

equipment.name: Stone Fist Elixir
entries: Your fists become hard as stone. For 1 hour, your fists deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage and lose the {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal} trait.

equipment.name: Storm Arrow
entries: The head of this arrow is made from gleaming copper. When an activated storm arrow hits a target, it's buffeted by raging winds and struck by a bolt of lightning that deals 3d12 electricity damage, and the target must attempt a DC 25 Reflex saving throw. If this arrow is shot from a weapon with a shock property rune, the save DC increases to 27, though the attack doesn't benefit from the {@i shock property} rune itself.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes half damage and isn't affected by the wind.
{@b Failure} The creature takes full damage and is buffeted by winds for 1 round, taking a –2 circumstance penalty to ranged attack rolls and a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its fly Speed.
{@b Critical Failure} As failure, but the creature takes double damage.

equipment.name: Striking Snare
entries: You affix a trip line or other trigger to a group of either stones or wooden stakes to strike a creature that enters the snare's square. The creature must attempt a DC 26 basic Reflex saving throw. If you choose stones when you {@action Craft|PC1} the snare, it deals 9d8 bludgeoning damage; if you choose spikes, it deals 9d8 piercing damage.

equipment.name: Stunning Snare
entries: You rig a snare to disorient a creature with a quick bash, leaving it with little ability to defend itself. The trap deals 10d6 bludgeoning damage to the first creature to enter its square; that creature must attempt a DC 32 Reflex save.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature takes half damage and is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} for 1 round and {@condition Stunned|PC1|stunned} 1.
{@b Failure} The creature takes full damage and is off-guard for 1 round and stunned 2.
{@b Critical Failure} The creature takes double damage and is off-guard for 1 minute and stunned 4.

equipment.name: Surging Serum
entries: Involuntary jolts and surges of energy move through the drinker's body as it restores normal muscle control. When you drink this elixir, it attempts to counteract each effect that's inflicting the {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} or {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled} condition on you, using the listed counteract rank and modifier.

equipment.name: Tangle Root Toxin
entries: Tangle root toxin sees use to impede opponents in athletic competitions, in addition to espionage and tracking.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 26 Fortitude; {@b Onset} 1 minute; {@b Maximum Duration} 6 minutes
{@b Stage 1} {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} 1 and –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 minute)
{@b Stage 2} clumsy 2 and –20- foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 minute)
{@b Stage 3} clumsy 3, {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}, and –30-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 minute)

equipment.name: Taper of Sanctification
entries: This thin golden candle bears the symbol of a specific deity emblazoned on its surface, surrounded by the iconography of that deity's faith. A {@i taper of sanctification} must be dedicated to a deity who can be sanctified to {@trait Holy|PC1|holy} or {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy}, and has the corresponding trait. If the deity's sanctification lists both options, the crafter must choose one when the candle is made.

Once lit, this candle burns for 1 hour, and it can't be extinguished. When a willing creature spends the full hour within 10 feet of the lit candle engaging in prayer to the deity, that creature's {@action Strike|PC1|Strikes} gain the holy or unholy trait (as appropriate for the candle) until the next time that creature makes their daily preparations. During this time, the creature is bound by the deity's anathema. If they violate anathema, they lose the benefit of the taper of sanctification. A holy creature can't benefit from an unholy taper of sanctification, nor can an unholy creature benefit from a holy one.

equipment.name: Tears of Death
entries: Tears of death are among the most powerful of alchemical poisons, distilled from extracts of five other deadly poisons in just the right ratios.
{@b Saving Throw} DC 44 Fortitude; {@b Onset} 1 minute; {@b Maximum Duration} 10 minutes; Stage 1 20d6 poison damage and {@condition Paralyzed|PC1|paralyzed} (1 round)
{@b Stage 2} 22d6 poison damage and paralyzed (1 minute)
{@b Stage 3} 24d6 poison damage and paralyzed (1 minute)

equipment.name: Terrifying Ammunition
entries: This black-and-gray ammunition is etched with occult symbols and tiny, grinning skulls. When activated {@i terrifying ammunition} damages a creature, the creature's mind is filled with visions of its failures, its tragedies, and eventually, its own death. The creature must attempt a DC 20 Will save.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature is {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened} 1.
{@b Failure} The creature is frightened 1 and can't reduce its frightened value below 1 until it spends an action, which has the {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate} trait, to calm itself down.
{@b Critical Failure} As failure, but the creature is frightened 2.

equipment.name: Timeless Salts
entries: You sprinkle these salts onto a single object up to 10 cubic feet in volume and no more than 40 Bulk to preserve it for 1 week. The object doesn't decay, and effects that require the object to be fresh don't count the time passing during this duration as having elapsed. When sprinkled on a corpse, this extends the period in which a creature can be revived by magic as well as the wait time required before a corpse can be targeted again with talking corpse. The salts prevent ordinary pests from consuming the target (such as maggots for a corpse or moths for a piece of clothing). Any creature can use an Interact action to disperse the salts from an unattended object and end this effect.

equipment.name: Tricky Liniment
entries: This greenish, persistent grease can be applied to armor to make it extremely slippery for 8 hours, granting the wearer a +2 item bonus to Acrobatics checks to {@action Escape|PC1} or to {@action Squeeze|PC1}.

equipment.name: Trip Snare
entries: You set a cunning wire to trip a creature. A Medium or smaller creature that enters this snare's square must attempt a DC 21 Reflex save.

If you want to create a trip snare to trip a larger creature, you must create a group of contiguous snares of a length equal to the edge of that larger creature's space, and the creature must be moving such that it moves into the full set of snares. For example, three trip snares in a 15-foot-line can trip a Huge creature coming down a corridor into the line of snares.
{@b Critical Success} The creature is unaffected.
{@b Success} The creature is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the start of its next turn.
{@b Failure} The creature falls {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}.
{@b Critical Failure} The creature falls prone and takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

equipment.name: Twisting Twine
entries: This ball of hempen twine resists efforts to unravel it by hand.

{@b Activate}{@b —Unravel Twine} {@as 1} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You toss the ball of twine into a square within 20 feet. The twine then unravels and animates, attempting to Disarm or Trip (your choice) a creature in the square with a total of +9 to the Athletics check. At the end of your turn, the twine winds itself back into a ball and returns to your hand; if you don't have a free hand, it returns to your space instead.

equipment.name: Unholy Plate
entries: Crafted from black iron, this crude suit of {@i +2 resilient {@equipment Full Plate|PC1|full plate}} is designed to make you look like a horned demon with your face peering out of the screaming maw of the beast.

While wearing the armor, you can attack with the helmet's horns. They're a martial melee weapon with the effects of a {@i +2 weapon potency rune}. They deal 2d8 piercing damage and have the {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly} d12 and {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy} traits. On a critical hit with the horns, the target must succeed at a DC 30 Fortitude or become {@condition Drained|PC1|drained} 1 (or drained 2 on a critical failure). The horns can't be etched with any runes.
If you're {@trait Holy|PC1|holy}, you're drained 2 and can't recover from this condition while wearing unholy plate.
{@b Activate}{@b —Demonic Slip} {@as 2} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You cast {@spell Translocate|PC1|translocate}.
{@b Craft Requirements} You’re unholy; supply one casting of {@spell Translocate|PC1|translocate}.

equipment.name: Urn of Ashes
entries: This pewter urn contains the ashes of a benevolent ancestor, with a sliver of lingering spirit that strives to protect you.

{@b Activate}{@b —Doom the Urn} {@as r} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}); {@b Trigger} You would become {@condition Doomed|PC1|doomed}, or your doomed value would increase; {@b Requirements} The ashes aren't doomed;; {@b Effect} The ashes in the urn intervene, taking the doomed condition in your place, and you don't gain or increase the value of your doomed condition. Each night when you get a full night's rest, you can reduce your own doomed condition or that of the urn, but not both.

{@b Activate}{@b —Spirit's Wrath} {@as 1} ({@trait Attack|PC1|attack}, {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}, {@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}); {@b Frequency} once per round; {@b Effect} The urn shoots a bolt of void energy at a foe within 30 feet. Attempt a spell attack roll against the target's AC, using a modifier of +15 or your own spell attack modifier, whichever is higher. On a success, the bolt deals 4d4 void damage (doubled on a critical success).

equipment.name: Viper Arrow
entries: The shaft of this arrow is covered in fine green scales, and its iron head comes to a pair of points almost like fangs. After an activated viper arrow hits a target, the arrow transforms into a {@creature Viper|MC1|viper}. The target is affected by the viper's venom, as if it had been bitten. The viper then lands in an open space adjacent to the target.

The viper has the {@trait Summoned|PC1|summoned} trait and acts at the end of your turn, even though you didn't use the {@action Sustain|PC1} action. It's under the GM's control, but it generally attacks the creature the arrow struck. The viper vanishes after 1 minute or when slain.
{@b Craft Requirements} Supply one casting of {@spell Summon Animal|PC1|summon animal}.

entries: This alabaster wand has a clear crystal at the tip.

equipment.name: Adze
entries: A common cutting tool, an adze resembles an axe—but the cutting edge is horizontal, rather than vertical. The adze’s shape makes it popular among woodworkers, and tripkee builders often use them to construct their treetop homes. The tool also serves as an effective weapon, due in part to the immense strength required to swing it.

equipment.name: Breaching Pike
entries: Forged with a heavy metal wedge effective at damaging enemy shields, breaching pikes are often used by hobgoblin infantry alongside a {@equipment Tower Shield|PC1|tower shield}.

equipment.name: Capturing Spetum
entries: Hobgoblins use these polearms both as standard issue for aggressive military units and on an individual basis for hunting fugitives.

equipment.name: Claw Blade
entries: This handheld weapon’s three parallel blades extend between the fingers to resemble the natural claws of the amurruns who created them, providing a way for those catfolk without suitable natural claws to share the fighting customs of their kin.

equipment.name: Cruuk
entries: This specialized club is designed for throwing and useful in both combat and hunting. Tripkees use them to take down creatures that hide high in treetops.

equipment.name: Fangwire
entries: This kobold wire is thin and hard to see, making it perfect for an ambush. The wielder flicks one handle around a vulnerable spot so that it serves as a catch for the wire, then yanks the other handle back, pulling the wire tight and inflicting painful lacerations. The function and name come from a wire-based trap called a “slow fang.”

equipment.name: Flying Talon
entries: This weapon consists of a three-pronged barbed hook attached to a length of chain. It can be used in melee to stab foes or hurled at a range. Some kobolds are particularly fond of using flying talons, especially as a sort of badge of office above those who serve them.

equipment.name: Hand Adze
entries: The adze’s smaller version is useful for delicate woodworking in cramped spaces. Tripkees use hand adzes for crafting and as close quarters weapons.

equipment.name: Khopesh
entries: This curved sickle sword has a pointed tip, allowing it to be swung in wide arcs or thrust vertically around enemy defenses. The tip of a khopesh is hooked and can be used to trip an opponent.

equipment.name: Mambele
entries: Also known as a hunga munga or danisco, this knife-axe hybrid consists of a hilt and blade that curves backward toward the wielder. The blade’s curve is such that, after a mambele has struck a victim, more damage is dealt as the weapon is extracted from the victim’s body.

equipment.name: Spirit Thresher
entries: Bones, some solid and others splintered, are affixed to metal chains at the end of a long stick to form a powerful flail. Many kholo warriors insist the vicious crack the weapon makes as it strikes loosens fragments of the soul like husks struck from grains.

equipment.name: Thunder Sling
entries: Tengu use these specialized slings to fire darts further and with greater force than when thrown by hand. A thunder sling uses {@equipment Dart|PC1|darts} as ammunition. It can also hurl {@equipment Blowgun Darts|PC1|blowgun darts} as ammunition but deals 1d4 piercing damage instead of 1d6 when used this way.

equipment.name: Tricky Pick
entries: This ingenious kobold pick conceals several hidden traps that the wielder can activate to trick and befuddle foes with a variety of damaging blades and bludgeoning surfaces.

equipment.name: Whip Claw
entries: The whip claw is a long tether affixed to claw-like daggers, allowing the wielder to fling and retract them with deadly precision. Catfolk first developed this weapon to provide extended reach when hunting dangerous animals, and they wield them with unmatched expertise.

equipment.name: Daikyu
entries: This asymmetrical bow, made of laminated bamboo, wood, and leather, stands 6 feet or more in height. It’s most often used while mounted.

equipment.name: Tengu Gale Blade
entries: This fan-shaped sword designed by tengu smiths has five broad blades that join at its hilt. Tengu sailors use them as makeshift weather vanes, for the sword spins in the wind’s direction when loosely held aloft.
